text: This is NetCoop AI: an evidence-seeking, multi-agent system that diagnoses network faults and explains why.
tts: This is NetCoop A.I.: an evidence-seeking, multi-agent system that diagnoses network faults, and explains why.

text: Built for the IIT Bhubaneswar Agentic AI challenge: specialist agents analyse telemetry, exchange structured findings, and agree on one evidence-backed diagnosis.
tts: It was built for the I.I.T. Bhubaneswar Agentic A.I. challenge. Specialist agents analyse telemetry, exchange structured findings, and agree on one evidence-backed diagnosis.

text: Network faults are distributed and ambiguous: a dead access point and a failed switch port can raise exactly the same alarms.
NetCoop gives each domain its own agent, tests every explanation against the topology and timeline, and asks for missing evidence when two explanations tie.
One investigation: validate the telemetry, analyse it in parallel, build competing hypotheses, request the deciding observation, then report.
On 60 held-out synthetic scenarios, 59 had an acceptable outcome versus 22 for a threshold baseline. These are internally generated scenarios, not real-world accuracy.
tts: On sixty held-out synthetic scenarios, fifty-nine had an acceptable outcome, versus twenty-two for a threshold baseline. These are internally generated scenarios, not real-world accuracy.

text: Let's open the Command Center.
The sidebar holds navigation, a scenario launcher, and live status of the coordinator and the three specialist agents, each a separate process.
We start with the organizer's own sample-generator data: a hardware failure on switch SW_CAMPUS_3.
tts: We start with data from the organizer's own sample generator: a hardware failure on switch S W campus 3.

text: Run diagnosis creates an incident, ingests the records, and starts the three agents over the A2A protocol.
tts: Run diagnosis creates an incident, ingests the records, and starts the three agents over the A to A protocol.

text: The data source is labelled truthfully: organizer data from the problem statement's sample generator, mapped by a declared source profile.
Fields the generator never defines, such as queue drops and status, are reported and not used. Nothing is guessed.
This diagram is the heart of the system: the incident fans out to three specialists working in parallel.
Performance found high latency and loss, Infrastructure found CPU at 99.9 percent, and Connectivity found nothing abnormal in its domain.
tts: The Performance agent found high latency and loss. The Infrastructure agent found C.P.U. at ninety-nine point nine percent. The Connectivity agent found nothing abnormal in its domain.

text: Their findings flow into the STEaR reasoner. The evidence was decisive, so no verification was needed.
tts: Their findings flow into the steer reasoner. The evidence was decisive, so no verification was needed.

text: Conclusion: device CPU overload at SW_CAMPUS_3, with moderate support, because all evidence comes from a single source.
tts: Conclusion: device C.P.U. overload at S W campus 3, with moderate support, because all of the evidence comes from a single source.

text: Confidence 0.88 is calibrated: conclusions of this kind were correct in 14 of 15 held-out cases. It is not a guessed percentage.
tts: The confidence, zero point eight eight, is calibrated: conclusions of this kind were correct in fourteen of fifteen held-out cases. It is not a guessed percentage.

text: The topology marks the faulted switch in red. The generator provides no topology, so this star layout is a labelled assumption.
Below: the persisted timeline, the competing hypotheses with why the leader wins, and a plain summary with actions for an operator.
Now evidence seeking: an access point is down, and the deciding data exists only in a wireless-controller archive.
We run it, and all three agents start in parallel again.
In round one STEaR was stuck: an access-point failure and a failed switch port predicted the same symptoms.
tts: In round one, steer was stuck: an access point failure and a failed switch port predicted the same symptoms.

text: Instead of guessing, it sent a targeted A2A verification task to the Infrastructure agent, asking only for the device status of AP-2-1.
tts: Instead of guessing, it sent a targeted A to A verification task to the Infrastructure agent, asking only for the device status of A P 2 1.

text: Twenty recorded observations came back, and round two concluded: device down at AP-2-1, high support, confidence 0.97.
tts: Twenty recorded observations came back, and round two concluded: device down at A P 2 1, with high support, and confidence zero point nine seven.

text: The topology now marks AP-2-1 as the root cause, with its impact scope highlighted.
tts: The topology now marks A P 2 1 as the root cause, with its impact scope highlighted.

text: The specialists are discovered live over A2A, with their skills, metrics and loopback-only endpoints.
tts: The specialists are discovered live over A to A, with their skills, metrics, and loopback-only endpoints.

text: Every exchange is persisted. Opening one shows the raw NDEP artifact exactly as the agent returned it, citing observation IDs.
tts: Every exchange is persisted. Opening one shows the raw N DEP artifact exactly as the agent returned it, citing observation I.D.s.

text: The reasoning page shows the decision basis, the ranking rule, and what changed round by round.
Every hypothesis is listed as confirmed, plausible, or ruled out by observed evidence, with its contradictions and missing discriminators.
The Evidence Explorer shows validated observations with explicit units, freshness and quality flags.
Each one traces back to the immutable raw record it came from, so every number in a report is auditable.
Datasets and Upload accepts NDEP JSON, vendor CSV through declared profiles, and the organizer's format.
tts: Datasets and upload accepts N DEP jason, vendor C S V through declared profiles, and the organizer's format.

text: This organizer scenario has deliberately corrupted records: a renamed field with the wrong unit, a missing device ID, a bad timestamp, an impossible value and a duplicate.
tts: This organizer scenario has deliberately corrupted records: a renamed field with the wrong unit, a missing device I.D., a bad timestamp, an impossible value, and a duplicate.

text: Each problem is reported record by record and never silently coerced. The diagnosis continues on the valid data and honestly reports an unknown fault.
The report is the schema-validated JSON the problem statement asks for: cause, evidence, affected devices, alternatives, confidence, actions and limitations.
tts: The report is the schema-validated jason the problem statement asks for: cause, evidence, affected devices, alternatives, confidence, actions, and limitations.

text: Limitations are stated in every report, including the scope of the confidence calibration.
The same report can be viewed as JSON and exported; a text version is available too.
tts: The same report can be viewed as jason and exported. A text version is available too.

text: Evaluation compares four methods on the held-out set, with the caveats first: synthetic data, same authors, not root-cause accuracy.
Full NetCoop has the most acceptable outcomes and no high-support mistakes; verification is what turns ambiguous cases into identified ones.
Settings shows the backend connection and readiness. A clearly labelled recorded preview works even without a backend.
Everything runs locally with one command, start.sh or start.ps1 on Windows. A verified release ZIP and a single-container Render image are included.
tts: Everything runs locally with one command: start dot S H, or start dot P S 1 on Windows. A verified release zip and a single-container Render image are included.

text: No LLM is required: the diagnosis is deterministic and tested, and every claim links to real evidence. Thank you for watching.
tts: No large language model is required. The diagnosis is deterministic and tested, and every claim links to real evidence. Thank you for watching NetCoop A.I.
